fc149bdda052a23ffe9a6a7bae0d8f71d08a8a5f.summary: This is a project README for godoh, a proof-of-concept command-and-control framework written in Go that uses DNS-over-HTTPS as its transport. It describes installation, build steps, command-line usage and a GPL v3 license. It is a software project page rather than a threat report, so it records no actors, incidents, CVEs or other threat facts.

fcdc48050d4a7d14d7fb3a7d181e8691472925e4.summary: CrowdStrike Intelligence overview of threats to VMware ESXi hypervisors. It says ransomware groups, including ransomware-as-a-service platforms, increasingly target ESXi, which does not support third-party antivirus. It cites exploited OpenSLP vulnerabilities (CVE-2020-3992, CVE-2021-21974), credential theft as the main entry route, a RAT ecosystem documented by Mandiant, and VM-escape exploit chains likely limited to advanced actors. It closes with defensive recommendations: jump servers with MFA, no internet exposure of vCenter, and offsite backups.

hedges: The report states its assessment that adversaries will likely keep targeting VMware virtualization infrastructure is made with high confidence.
The report says VM-escape exploit chains need several exploits, no public proof-of-concept exists as of writing, and only advanced actors likely have the capability.
The report says none of the cross-site scripting vulnerabilities are known to be exploited in the wild, and it is not aware of exploitation of CVE-2021-22043.
The report cites industry reporting that credential theft appears to be the primary attack vector against ESXi servers.
The report notes VMware has deprecated its knowledge base article on third-party agents and antivirus on ESXi as outdated.
The report defines high confidence as not implying absolute certainty; such judgments still carry a marginal probability of being inaccurate.
